text:
maria: Heads up — eu-west-1 spot shortage this morning, lots of A100s reclaimed. Our inference p99s jumped for a few minutes. Anyone seen this pattern elsewhere?
aj: yep, noticed reclaims around 09:18–09:25 UTC, autoscaler replaced nodes but binpacking got messy. Some pods drifted to smaller GPUs and throttled.

kai: we should consider widening the instance mix for the spot pool. Right now it's A100-only which is brittle.
sarah: agreed. proposal: add L4 and A10G to the pool, use capacity-aware binpacking so big models stay on high-memory GPUs.
maria: +1 on capacity-aware placement. Also region fallback: if eu-west1 is saturated, route non-SLA batch jobs to eu-central or on-demand pool.

aj: tradeoffs: L4 is cheap per-token but lower throughput for large seq lengths. A100/H100 have better throughput for long seqs. We need scoring function: cost_per_token, throughput, eviction_rate.

kai: sketch of placement policy (pseudo):
```
if model.mem > 40GB -> prefer A100/H100 pool
elif latency_sensitive and batch_size < 8 -> prefer L4 (lower cost, good single-stream)
else -> A10G for cheaper mid-tier
apply spot_eviction_risk_penalty to score
```

infra-bot: InterruptNotice: spotted termination events on i-spot-a100-*

aj: interruption handling: we should ensure graceful drains and quick failover to smaller supertypes. Suggested: 1) checkpoint KV cache to Redis every 30s for long-running streams, 2) have warm standby nodes in dedicated pool for critical routes, 3) quick model fallback to quantized variant.

sarah: also recommend multi-queue scheduler: "latency-sla" vs "best-effort". Best-effort jobs can be spill-to-spot-europe or queued. Latency-sla routes to dedicated or low-eviction spot types.
maria: curious about cross-zone traffic cost for fallback to other region — it's nontrivial. We should prefer intra-region fallback (eu-central) first.

kai: question: do we run one mixed ASG per region or multiple ASGs per GPU class? Pros/cons?
aj: mixed ASG (multi-instance-type) keeps single scaling decision, better binpacking. Multiple ASGs simpler policy but harder to rebalance. I prefer mixed ASG with per-instance weights and pod nodeAffinity.
sarah: weight idea: set capacityWeight = vGPU_equivalent * (1 - eviction_score). That lets autoscaler prefer stable types while still allowing cheap ones.

maria: can ops run a short experiment? split 20% capacity to mixed L4/A10G, 80% A100 for a week and collect p50/p99, cost/token, eviction_count.

aj: I'll create a small canary: 10 nodes mixed pool in eu-west1, attach a subset of test routes (non-critical). Will push script today.

kai: thanks — please post results in #eng-infra. If eviction_score remains high, we shift more SLA traffic to dedicated.
maria: ack. one more: ensure our rollout includes model quantization fallback test in the eval harness so we don't silently degrade quality when falling back.

infra-bot: DeployJob started by aj at 11:40 UTC — creating canary mixed-spot pool (eu-west-1).

aj: logs from canary setup:
```
2026-03-18T11:41:05Z create-asg --types [a100,l4,a10g] --weights [1.0,0.25,0.5]
2026-03-18T11:41:09Z attach-nodegroup test-canary-spot
2026-03-18T11:41:22Z autoscaler: scale_to 10
```

kai: nice. let's monitor eviction_rate and per-route latency. If stable after 48h we can expand to 50%.
sarah: also add a metric: percent_requests_served_by_quantized_fallback so we can trace quality/regression.

maria: perfect. tagging @product for visibility — this impacts SLOs. :eyes:
